correctness.rationale: The kernel equation x_(i+1)=x_i+x_(i-1) mod2 has exactly four period-3 solutions when 3|n and only zero otherwise. The image is the codimension-two equality of three parity sums. For a fixed output y of least period p, the necklace predecessor classes are stabilizer R^p orbits on its 4-member labeled fiber. When 3 does not divide p, action has one fixed and one 3-cycle, giving 2. When 3|p and primitive block is reachable, action fixes all 4; otherwise it translates by nonzero 2-torsion, giving 2. Burnside uses H_n(d) fixed reachable strings; Mobius inversion on primitive good blocks yields B4. I independently enumerated all labeled inputs and quotient output fibers for n=1..12, confirming the exact (B0,B2,B4) histograms (2,2,0), (8,5,1), (44,2,14), (256,16,80) at n=3,6,9,12. The nontrivial all-n argument rests on group action/linear algebra, not this finite run.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete invariant of the rotation-quotient dynamics: it distinguishes 0,2,4 predecessor necklaces despite all reachable labeled outputs having four predecessors. Exact period/parity criteria, census formulas and almost-sure degree-four asymptotics aid classification of finite cyclic cellular-automaton phase space. It is not a mere renaming of labeled linear rank.

final_claim: For synchronous F_n(x)_i=x_(i-1) xor x_i xor x_(i+1) modulo binary spatial rotations, inverse necklace degree is 1 for 3 not dividing n, and for 3 dividing n it equals 0 when three residue-class parities disagree, 4 if reachable and the primitive block (period divisible by 3) is itself locally reachable, otherwise 2. Exact Mobius-Burnside formula enumerates all classes, and degree 4 is asymptotically prevalent among reachable classes.
